text: Seabrook Town a gagné 4-2 contre Harbour City grâce à un match plein d’émotions et de buts spectaculaires [#905] [#975] [#1104] [#1448] [#1882] [#1906]. Harbour City a bien commencé avec deux buts rapides, un superbe but d’Elias Okafor à la 45e minute après une longue série de 17 passes, et un second de Marek Barros sur corner [#905] [#975]. Mais Seabrook Town, grâce à sa tactique de pressing haut et jeu direct, a su égaliser et marquer trois fois en seconde période, notamment avec Kian Romano qui a inscrit un doublé dans le temps ajouté, offrant la victoire à son équipe [#1361] [#1882] [#1906]. Avec 22 tirs contre 10 et un xG de 3.87 (qui indique que leurs chances valaient presque 4 buts), Seabrook a montré sa supériorité offensive, malgré la belle prestation de Marek Barros côté Harbour City, élu joueur du match pour ses passes clés et son but. Le carton rouge reçu par Joon Whitfield a aussi compliqué la tâche de Harbour City [#871].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals compared to Harbour City’s 2, winning the match 4-2 [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].  
- Marek Barros was player of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, 9 interceptions, and a 10.0 rating [team_stats].  
- Seabrook Town had higher xG of 3.87 vs Harbour City’s 1.82 and took more shots (22 vs 10) and shots on target (9 vs 5) [team_stats].  
- Harbour City played patient short passing in a 4-2-3-1, while Seabrook Town used a wide, crossing 3-4-3 style [team_styles].  
- Red card to Joon Whitfield at 43' likely affected Harbour City’s gameplay [#871].

- Harbour City's opening goal (45') came from a well-constructed patient short passing build-up involving 17 passes over nearly 57 seconds starting from open play, reflecting their 4-2-3-1 formation and style of patient possession to unlock defenses. Marek Barros provided a through ball assist to Elias Okafor who scored from close range (1.4m) [#905].

- The second goal for Harbour City (47') was from a corner, indicating effective exploitation of set pieces. Marek Barros, key in both build-up and scoring (via a cross), shows how their full-backs or wide attackers influence by crossing in their formation [#975].

- Seabrook Town's first goal (53'), scored by Tariq Marlowe within only 1 second and no intervening passes, followed an immediate regain of possession. This suggests a pressing trap or high-intensity defensive action typical of their 3-4-3 formation which emphasizes wide pressing and quick transitions [#1104].

- Seabrook's tactical change around minute 65 shifted them to press higher and play more direct, increasing their line height and press intensity. This enabled them to create 3 big chances in the second half and capitalize with goals from quick regain and direct through passes, exploiting their wide crossing style and forward positioning [#1361, #1448].

- Late goals around 90+2' and 90+3' from Seabrook were rapid counter-attacks and open play moves starting from regains, involving few passes and exploiting turnovers with quick through balls to Kian Romano, reflecting their directness and pressing leading to high turnovers (25 for them vs 13 for Harbour) [#1882, #1906].

- Harbour City's approach of patient possession and short passing (81.8% pass accuracy) contrasts with Seabrook's wide, crossing play (3-4-3 formation) that emphasizes more direct attacking, pressing and crossing, explaining the shift in momentum after Seabrook increased press and directness in the second half [#team_styles, #1361].
